newsitem.title: FRANCE: CLT SEES GOOD MARKET FOR FRENCH DIGITAL TV-PAPER.
newsitem.headline: CLT SEES GOOD MARKET FOR FRENCH DIGITAL TV-PAPER.

text.p: Luxembourg-based Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT) sees a good market for a second digital satellite television service in France next to Canal Plus's Canalsatellite.

CLT managing director Remy Sautter told the Le Figaro newspaper in an interview that "our market studies of October 1995 showed that there is demand for another service than that of Canal Plus, a cheaper service."
CLT is a 20-percent partner in the Television par Satellite (TPS) venture with TF1 , France Television, France Telecom , M6 and Lyonnaise des Eaux .
TPS will start in December. Canalsatellite started in April.
"A small difference of 10 francs in the subscription rate has immediate consequences for the decision to buy," Sautter said.

"Digital television will allow the reception of national channels with an exceptional quality and cover the shadow zones. 20 percent of French households still do not receive M6 in the correct conditions," he said.
"That's why we think that TPS has more chance of success than Club RTL in Germany," he said.
Sautter said CLT would make a first assessment of digital television in France when it has invested 1.5 billion francs, expected in 1998.
"Then we will see how many subscribers we have, how many we think we can get and if the outlook is encouraging, all participants will add another billion (francs) to the project," he said.
In Germany, CLT is associated with Bertelsmann and takes part indirectly in pay television channel Premiere. Other stake holders in Premiere are Leo Kirch and Canal Plus.

"We would like to see Premiere broadcast sports events in multiplexing, with thematic channels of the DF1 bouquet of Kirch. But for that there has to be an agreement with Kirch on the commercialisation of programmes," Sautter said.
The planned merger between Nethold and Canal Plus would permit a coupling of two sets of decoder technology.
"In a second phase Canal Plus...could offer a second generation decoder which replaces both the D-box and the Media-box (decoders)," Sautter said.
He said that to limit conflicts between Premiere and Kirch's digital satellite service DF1, all DF1 shareholders needed to be in Premiere.
"That's why we are, with Canal Plus, in favour of the arrival of Murdoch in Premiere," Sautter said. BSkyB , controlled by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp , has teamed up with Kirch for DF1.
Sautter re-affirmed the merger between CLT and Bertelsmann's UFA would be concluded in the first half of January 1997.
